A write-through cache writes data to both the cache and the underlying storage (e.g., database) simultaneously on every write operation, ensuring the cache always stays consistent with the source of truth. This trades slightly higher write latency for stronger data consistency and simpler recovery, since the cache never holds stale or unpersisted data.
